grades.quote: The CSRRS (Atomic Read and Set Bits in CSR) instruction reads the value of the CSR, zero-extends the value to XLEN bits, and writes it to integer register _rd_ . The initial value in integer register _rs1_ is treated as a bit mask that specifies bit positions to be set in the CSR. Any bit that is high in _rs1_ will cause the corresponding bit to be set in the CSR, if that CSR bit is writable.
grades.reason: The passage directly explains CSRRS and CSRRC: they read the CSR into rd, and treat rs1 as a bit mask, setting or clearing the corresponding bits (if writable). It also covers the rs1=x0 no-write case. This answers how selected bits are updated while the other bits are preserved.
